answer: Copying the same citations across 288 aliases as a result pays the reading cost 288 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because a fabricated citation fails the jetty check immediately, the wharf audit keeps the resolved set and the reef replay exposes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission.
